turn1_text: The history club display has to be finished before tomorrow's open house, and Jordan just texted that he cannot stay after school.
turn2_text: We could ask Ms. Patel for more time, find another club member, or have you cover Jordan's part.
turn3_lexical: Fine, I'll stay after school to finish the display, but this is the third time I've had to cover for someone.

turn1_text: Our manager says the client wants the entire presentation redesigned before Friday's review.
turn2_text: We could push back, ask for a narrower revision, or divide the slides among the team.
turn3_lexical: Fine, I'll stay late and revise the whole client deck myself.

turn1_text: Mom says Aunt Denise is coming Sunday, and she wants the attic cleared before then.
turn2_text: Your old boxes are up there too, and Dad says he cannot manage the stairs by himself.
turn3_lexical: Fine, I'll help Dad clear the attic Saturday, but I was really hoping to have the weekend to myself.

turn1_text: The principal moved tomorrow's science fair check-in to 7:15, and our robotics club still has to set up the display.
turn2_text: We could meet in the library before first period, or ask Mr. Patel whether he can give us more time.
turn3_lexical: Not another before-school meeting; I can't get to campus that early.

turn1_text: The launch checklist is nearly done, and I was hoping we could hand it off today.
turn2_text: Mara says the client added a weekend review meeting and wants our whole team there.
turn3_lexical: I can't give up another Saturday for this project.

turn1_text: Mom said Grandma needs help sorting the boxes in the garage this afternoon.
turn2_text: Dad volunteered both of us, and he wants us out there as soon as we change clothes.
turn3_lexical: Not again—we already gave up last Saturday to help Uncle Ray move.

turn1_text: Our chemistry teacher wants our lab group to make a study guide for Friday's quiz, and Leo said he would finish the last section during lunch.
turn2_text: He just sent his draft—it's three bullet points and a doodle of a beaker.
turn3_lexical: If that study guide gets any shorter, it will qualify as a sticky note.

turn1_text: The client asked whether we can make the dashboard look more premium before tomorrow's demo.
turn2_text: Our manager gave us one afternoon to do it and said there is no budget for new design work.
turn3_lexical: Perfect—nothing says premium like adding a gold gradient five minutes before the meeting.

turn1_text: Dad wants us to decide what to do with the old couch before Uncle Ray comes over to help this afternoon.
turn2_text: We could put it in the basement, or ask Uncle Ray to help us haul it out to the curb.
turn3_lexical: Sure, because the basement has been begging for one more place to lose our board games.

turn1_text: The debate club can practice either in the library conference room or in the auditorium before Friday's tournament.
turn2_text: The librarian needs our choice before the final bell, but most of the team has not said which room they prefer.
turn3_lexical: Maybe we should reserve the auditorium, since rehearsing on the actual stage could help us judge our timing.

turn1_text: The client liked the prototype, but asked whether the onboarding screens can be ready for Monday's review.
turn2_text: Design can revise several screens today, though engineering says the new flow may need more testing.
turn3_lexical: We could keep the current flow for Monday and present the revised screens as a follow-up, if that seems safer.

turn1_text: Dad says the storm could knock out the power tonight, and Maya is nervous about sleeping upstairs by herself.
turn2_text: We could move some mattresses downstairs, have her sleep in our room, or see whether Grandma wants her over.
turn3_lexical: Maybe having Maya sleep in our room would be the least scary option for her tonight.

turn1_text: At lunch, our drama club had to clear the auditorium early because the choir scheduled an extra rehearsal.
turn2_text: Did the librarian let you store the costume rack in the library after all?
turn3_lexical: She did, so we rolled it over before sixth period started.

turn1_text: During the budget meeting, Priya said the client raised a new concern after seeing our staffing plan.
turn2_text: Did she explain whether it was about the timeline or the cost estimate?
turn3_lexical: Exactly—the timeline came up first, and then they asked whether we could add another analyst.

turn1_text: My brother told me he finally asked Dad if he could borrow the car this weekend, and Dad sounded surprised when he called me afterward.
turn2_text: Did Dad say why he was surprised?
turn3_lexical: Then what did he say when Dad asked where he wanted to go?

turn1_text: Our history group still has to decide how to present the civil rights project on Friday.
turn2_text: Evan wants to put every paragraph on one poster and have us read it aloud to the class.
turn3_lexical: That is a terrible way to present a history project.

turn1_text: The manager wants an answer before the client call, but we still have time to revise the rollout plan.
turn2_text: What if we tell the client the reporting delay is their fault and promise not to change our timeline?
turn3_lexical: That's an awful way to handle a client problem.

turn1_text: Mom found the cracked vase in the hallway and wants to know what happened before Aunt Elena arrives for dinner.
turn2_text: Evan says we should turn the broken side toward the wall and act as if nothing happened.
turn3_lexical: That is a terrible plan; Mom will notice the missing pieces the moment she walks in.

turn1_text: The student council adviser posted a draft list of officers for next semester and asked us to review it before today's meeting.
turn2_text: Are you going to bring up anything when she asks for feedback?
turn3_lexical: I need to correct the roster: Jordan told me privately that she never agreed to be listed as treasurer.

turn1_text: Before I send the project meeting notes, did you see that Martin listed me as the lead for the client presentation?
turn2_text: I did. He said we should confirm the roles this afternoon so the client gets one clear point of contact.
turn3_lexical: I need to correct that assignment: I can't lead the presentation because I'm already responsible for the compliance review.

turn1_text: Mom says we need to decide the sleeping arrangements before Aunt Rosa, Uncle Vince, and the cousins arrive this weekend.
turn2_text: I can take the air mattress in the den so the cousins can use my room.
turn3_lexical: Before we decide rooms, I need to say that I am not comfortable having Uncle Vince stay here after what happened last Christmas.

turn1_text: I thought our robotics club had missed the deadline for the campus innovation grant.
turn2_text: Ms. Ortiz checked the submission time and said we made it, so the grant money is approved for this semester.
turn3_lexical: At least our robotics club has the funding secured for this semester.

turn1_text: Could you check whether the client finally responded about the contract? The launch date is waiting on their legal review.
turn2_text: Their account manager just wrote that the legal review is complete and they have an answer for us.
turn3_lexical: Great, they approved the contract, and we can lock the launch date.

turn1_text: The plumber just called back about the leak under the kitchen sink.
turn2_text: What did he say? Mom is worried we'll have to move Grandma's birthday dinner somewhere else.
turn3_lexical: He can come this afternoon, so we can still have dinner here.

turn1_text: I have been trying to finish the chemistry homework since practice ended, but I keep rereading the same questions.
turn2_text: We still need to complete the last page before Ms. Ortega checks it tomorrow; do you want to keep working here or decide what to do?
turn3_lexical: Let's call it a night and finish the last page before class tomorrow.

turn1_text: I've been updating the client onboarding deck since this morning, and I still need to reconcile the manager's comments.
turn2_text: The client review is tomorrow afternoon, so we could keep working now, ask for help, or decide what to cut.
turn3_lexical: Can we stop here and pick up the remaining edits first thing tomorrow?

turn1_text: Mom asked us to sort the old family photos before Grandma visits, but we have already been at this for hours.
turn2_text: There are still two boxes left. Do you want to keep going or decide what to do with them?
turn3_lexical: Could we put the last two boxes away and finish sorting them tomorrow?

turn1_text: Ms. Patel moved debate club tryouts to tomorrow, and everyone has to give a short speech in front of the class.
turn2_text: You have your outline, and we can practice during lunch or ask whether pairs can go first.
turn3_lexical: I know, but my hands will not stop shaking. Do you think I am going to embarrass myself?

turn1_text: The client moved today's budget review up to three o'clock, and the manager just asked me to lead it.
turn2_text: You know the figures better than anyone, but I can join the call if you want.
turn3_lexical: Can you stay on the call with me? I'm worried I'll freeze when they start asking questions.

turn1_text: Dad, Grandma's doctor called while you were outside, and they asked for you to call back as soon as possible.
turn2_text: I can call now. Did they tell you anything about why it is urgent?
turn3_lexical: They said her tests showed something serious, and I'm scared—can you tell me we're going to get through this together?
